summary: Willamette NF lookout in Lane County: camp from 1912, cabin from 1921, L-4 ground cabin built 1939, removed 1968; only concrete pillars remain.

facts.status_note: Removed in 1968 per the Forest Service; only concrete pillars remain

staffing.status: lookouts named in several summers from 1916 to 1934; no end-of-staffing date found

access.note: Reached by Hardesty Trail #3469, a Forest Service hiking trail; a recreation pass is required at the lower trailhead. The lookout itself is gone.

visit.trail_note: About 5 miles one way to the summit from the lower trailhead; upper trailhead on Forest Road 550; trees partly block the view; check current conditions with the local ranger station

events.note: Camp set up on the summit; an alidade was established for locating fires
John Cain returned to his lookout on Hardesty
Nell Southworth returned to Eugene from her post as fire lookout on Hardesty
Ready-cut lookout house shipped to Reserve in 1921, packed up by mule and erected by Ranger C.B. McFarland; register and Rex's page list a D-6 cupola cabin for 1921
Mrs. Walter Allan, formerly Nell Southworth, was the lookout
J. N. Smithson employed as lookout during the 1923 fire season
Smithson reported smoke from a new fire eight miles away; it was a small fire built by four or five railroad laborers
Smithson employed on Hardesty through the summer of 1930
W. P. Sheridan and his wife spent the balance of the summer at the lookout
CCC built a 14x14 L-4 ground cabin to replace the earlier cabin
Listed as activated for the Eugene Filter Center from August 11, 1942 to September 22, 1943
Forest Service, register and Forest Lookouts page say removed in 1968; Rex's page says destroyed that year
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on December 19, 2010

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Service says a lookout was in place from 1920; the register and Rex's page date the D-6 cupola cabin to 1921. The story dates the cabin to 1921 and notes the earlier Forest Service date.
The register, the Forest Service and the Forest Lookouts page say removed in 1968; Rex's page says destroyed that year. The story reports both wordings.

notes_for_editor: The weebly page has more dated staffing entries than the story uses. The Eugene Filter Center activation comes only from the Forest Lookouts page and no source read explains its role, so the story states the dates without interpretation. The access level 'public' is inferred from the Forest Service trail page (open trail, recreation pass at the lower trailhead) rather than from a closure notice; the brief said access unknown, and this record now applies only to the trail. No photos with usable image URLs were found.
